clue.text: Witty colonel drinking mineral

indicators.note: the colonel's letters take the mineral in, as a drinker takes in liquid

parts.note: COL is the standard abbreviation for the military rank of colonel
mica is a mineral that splits into thin glittering sheets

explanation.surface: An amusing army officer knocking back mineral water.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something witty is funny and amusing.

clue.text: Disasters involving upper-class holidays at sea

indicators.note: the disasters' word wraps round the letter, involving it

parts.note: crises are disasters

explanation.surface: Posh holidays on ships that ended in calamity.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a cruise is a pleasure voyage on a ship.

clue.text: Brave person, a Democrat, following heart — frequently moderate, politically?

indicators.note: the hero, a and Democrat come after the heart and frequently pieces

parts.note: the middle of something is its heart
oft is an old word for often, frequently
a hero is a brave person

explanation.surface: A political profile of a brave Democrat with centrist views.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a centrist politician avoids extremes of left or right.

clue.text: Messenger, out of uniform, going round with culinary herb

indicators.note: the shortened messenger goes round the synonym of with
the uniform letter is taken out of the messenger

parts.note: a courier is a messenger
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
and can mean with, as in 'fish and chips'

explanation.surface: A courier out of uniform doing his rounds with herbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' drops the uniform letter from the messenger, giving CORIER, and 'going round' wraps that round the word for with. 'out of uniform' reads as off duty, which hides the deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: coriander, also called cilantro, is a herb used in cooking.

clue.text: Unattached miss holding ring

indicators.note: the synonym of miss holds the ring letter inside it

parts.note: to lose out on something is to miss it
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A single woman holding an engagement ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miss' looks like a young woman, but it is the verb meaning fail to get.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something loose is unfastened or free.

clue.text: Eccentric learner driver, a Parisian with a twitch

parts.note: L is the learner plate on a British learner driver's car
a Parisian would say 'un' for 'a', the French indefinite article
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A twitchy French learner driver with odd habits.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, an eccentric is a wildly odd person, loosely a madman.

clue.text: Enjoy nuts greatly

parts.note: to like something is to enjoy it
nuts means crazy

explanation.surface: Someone is very fond of nuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal idiom: doing something madly means doing it to a great degree.

clue.text: Martial art expert's home in New Jersey area

indicators.note: the home word goes inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: NJ is the postal abbreviation for New Jersey
in means at home

explanation.surface: A martial arts expert lives in New Jersey.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a ninja was a Japanese warrior trained in stealthy martial arts.

clue.text: Suffer defeat stoically, as most boxers do?

definitions.meaning: to accept a setback bravely, without complaint
boxers literally take punches to the jaw

explanation.surface: Accepting a loss bravely, like a boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom from boxing: to absorb a blow to the jaw and keep going, hence to bear misfortune bravely.

clue.text: Items of cut glass? Shed tears, booth having only one left

parts.note: to cry is to shed tears

indicators.note: the booth word keeps only one of its two L letters

parts.note: a stall is a booth at a market

explanation.surface: Someone weeps at a stall selling cut glass, with only one left.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark is because 'crystal' is a collective noun for such glassware rather than a plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Collective sense: crystal is fine glassware, often decorated by cutting.

clue.text: Cranky duke, led on, wrongly imprisoned

indicators.note: the letters of these three words are set out wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered duke, deceived, was locked up unjustly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' looks like it qualifies 'imprisoned' (a miscarriage of justice), but it is the anagram signal for CRANKY DUKE LED ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something kept locked away securely, or a person held in prison.

clue.text: When young woman briefly returned for a dance

indicators.note: coming back means the combined letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: a lass is a young woman

explanation.surface: Someone came back to dance just when a girl was there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts the girl's word to LAS, and 'returned' reverses the whole ASLAS. 'When' looks like a time link but supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: salsa is a lively Latin American dance.

clue.text: Service his curate arranged

indicators.note: the letters of these two words are arranged in a new order

explanation.surface: A curate organised a church service of his own.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Holy Communion is a church service of bread and wine.

clue.text: At the moment, assume one is in South American national park

indicators.note: the group of synonyms sits inside the two abbreviation letters

parts.note: S for South and A for American
now means at the moment
to don something is to put it on, to assume it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A traveller wonders about a national park in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American' looks like it places the park, but it only supplies two letters to wrap round the rest. Snowdonia is in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Snowdonia, or Eryri, is a mountainous national park in north Wales.

clue.text: Song, for example, right to be included by tenors performing

indicators.note: the right and example letters are included inside the reworked word
the letters of tenors perform, moving into a new order

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation of exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: Tenors performing a song, for instance, with the right note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performing' turns the singers' word into NORETS; 'for example' looks like it introduces an instance of a song but supplies two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: 'Non, je ne regrette rien', Edith Piaf's song, is known in English by this title.

clue.text: Lower hood after onset of shower

indicators.note: the hood follows the opening letter
the start of the word shower gives its first letter

parts.note: a cowl is a monk's hood

explanation.surface: Pulling a hood down when a shower starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' reads as 'pull down' but is the verb pronounced to rhyme with 'flower': to frown.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword-friendly sense: to lour or lower is to frown sullenly.

clue.text: One watches Wall of Sound producer tackling a tango

indicators.note: the producer's name takes on the pair of letters, grappling them inside

parts.note: Phil Spector was the record producer famed for the 'Wall of Sound'
T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone observes a famous record producer attempting a tango.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a spectator is an onlooker who watches an event.

clue.text: Put off head of team feeding animals

indicators.note: something fed into the animals goes inside their word

parts.note: deer are animals

indicators.note: the top letter of the word team

explanation.surface: A team leader was discouraged from feeding the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to put someone off doing something is to discourage them.

clue.text: Desperately determined in entrance and exit

parts.note: a door is an entrance
to exit can mean to die, as in exit this life

explanation.surface: Someone is frantic to get in and out.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an all-or-nothing attempt, ready to risk everything.

clue.text: Would-be poet met merry with sherry!

indicators.note: tipsy or merry means the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: An aspiring poet got tipsy on sherry.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhymester is a writer of trivial verse, a poetaster rather than a true poet.

clue.text: Letter I posted contains quick and clever reply

indicators.note: the phrase holds the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: A letter I sent included a witty comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a riposte is a sharp retort, originally a fencing counter-thrust.

clue.text: Innocent mistake concerning vision

parts.note: over can mean concerning, as in 'a row over money'
sight is vision

explanation.surface: An honest error about someone's eyesight.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an oversight is an unintended slip or omission.

clue.text: Twenty, the full total

definitions.meaning: a group of twenty, as in 'threescore years and ten'
the total of points in a game, as in the final tally

explanation.surface: Twenty is the whole amount.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a set of twenty, and the points tally in a game.

clue.text: Jewellery item, article collected by rising Italian artist

indicators.note: the article is collected inside the other letters
in a down clue, rising means the Italian abbreviation is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: IT is a short form for Italian, as in gin and it (Italian vermouth)
RA is Royal Academician, an artist
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An Italian artist on the up collects a piece of jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns the Italian abbreviation upwards into TI, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a tiara is a jewelled headpiece, like a small crown.

clue.text: Secure, having connection at university

parts.note: a tie is a connection or link
in British usage, up means in residence at university, as in 'up at Oxford'

explanation.surface: Someone gets a place through contacts at their university.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb: to tie up a boat or a deal is to secure it.

clue.text: Imitate Cockney at speech indoors, badly

indicators.note: these letters are put together badly, in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: Doing a bad Cockney voice while giving a speech indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, famously leave out the H sound, saying 'ouse' for 'house'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: leaving out the H sound at the start of words is typical of Cockney speech.

clue.text: Tiresomely long finish, not so great

parts.note: an end is a finish
less means smaller in amount, not so great

explanation.surface: A dragged-out ending that was a letdown.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyperbole: something tedious seems to go on with no conclusion.

clue.text: Set out from Scottish island, gillie initially heading for England

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde, Scotland

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word gillie is taken
the head, or first letter, of the word England is taken too

explanation.surface: A Highland hunting guide leaves a Scottish island bound for England.
explanation.walkthrough: A gillie is a guide for hunting or fishing in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to set out items is to lay them in order.
